claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I do. I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm assessing eligibility for your son Alex, who is 17 and lives with you in the UK.

Since Alex is 17 (over 16), I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, studying at school, college, or in an approved training program)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school but hasn't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 17 and not in approved education or training, I need to understand his current situation:

**Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services after leaving education?** (If yes, when did he register?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with anything like that. He just finished school and has been at home since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I need one more piece of information:

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's just been at home taking a break since finishing school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me ask one final question to complete my assessment:

**How long ago did Alex finish school/leave education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He finished school about two months ago.

conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can continue if they are under 20 **and** stay in approved education or training. Since Alex is 17 but is not currently in approved education or training, the standard eligibility criteria are not met.

There is an exception that allows Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service, or
- The armed services

However, Alex has not registered with either of these services since leaving school two months ago.

**What Alex could do:** If Alex registers with a government-sponsored careers service now, this may allow you to claim Child Benefit for a 20-week period. You may want to look into this option and contact the Child Benefit Office for guidance on whether backdating would be possible given his circumstances.

I hope this information is helpful, even though it's not the outcome you were hoping for.
